c.tagline: Sprawling, diverse, and hungry - space city with a world of food.

taxi.fareNote: Metered fares start around $2.91 by day and $3.91 at night with roughly $2.31 per mile; most cabs take cards but carry cash as a backup. Flat-rate zones apply from the airports.

emergency.note: 911 is the single emergency number for police, fire, and ambulance across the United States.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

avoid.reason: Caution in some southern/eastern neighborhoods; downtown/tourist areas fine

hood_desc: The compact business and sports core, home to the Theater District, Discovery Green, Minute Maid Park, and Toyota Center; best for first-timers who want to be central, walkable, and on the METRORail Red Line.

Houston's bohemian, LGBTQ-friendly arts district of leafy streets, indie boutiques, tattoo parlors, galleries, and some of the city's best restaurants and bars; suits travelers wanting character and nightlife.

A cultural cluster of 19 museums including the Museum of Fine Arts, Houston Museum of Natural Science, and the Menil Collection, ringed by parks and the Hermann Park green space; ideal for culture-focused visitors.

A historic, tree-lined neighborhood of restored Victorian bungalows, the walkable 19th Street shopping strip, hike-and-bike trails, and buzzy farm-to-table dining; a calmer, local base just north of Downtown.
A dense, energetic district just south of Downtown packed with bars, patios, restaurants, and young professionals; connected by the METRORail Red Line and best for nightlife and dining.
lodging: Best Western Plus Downtown Inn & Suites
La Quinta Inn by Wyndham Houston Greenway Plaza Medical Area
Howard Johnson by Wyndham Houston Downtown

water.note: Tap water is safe to drink citywide.

transit.hours: METRORail runs roughly 4:30am to midnight (later on weekends); local buses vary, with several routes running early morning to late night.
transit.note: Houston is car-oriented, but METRORail and local buses cover Downtown, Midtown, the Museum District, and the Medical Center well.
transit.pay: Tap a contactless bank card or phone, or use the RideMETRO fare card (which replaced the METRO Q Card in early 2026). The local bus, METRORail, and curb2curb fare is $1.25, and every 11th trip is free after 10 paid trips.

transit.m: METRO Route 102 Bush IAH Express bus to Downtown (~45 min)

tip.r: ~18-20% at restaurants; tipping is expected across US service industries.

food.name: Tex-Mex fajitas
food.desc: Marinated skirt steak grilled over high heat, sliced and served sizzling with flour tortillas, guacamole and charro beans. Houston claims the invention.

places.name: The Original Ninfa's on Navigation
places.note: Mama Ninfa put fajitas on the American menu here in 1973; handmade tortillas still.

places.name: El Tiempo Cantina
places.note: Run by the Laurenzo family; huge fajita platters and famously strong margaritas.

places.name: Pappasito's Cantina
places.note: Houston-born chain locals still rate for mesquite-grilled beef and shrimp fajitas.

food.name: Viet-Cajun crawfish
food.desc: Boiled crawfish tossed in garlic butter loaded with lemongrass, chili and butter. Born in Houston's Vietnamese community; eat with gloves, January to June.

places.name: Crawfish and Noodles
places.note: Chef Trong Nguyen's James Beard-recognized spot; the dish's most cited home.

places.name: Cajun Kitchen
places.note: Bellaire Boulevard favorite for whole boils, garlic noodles and fried catfish.

places.name: LA Crawfish
places.note: Casual mini-chain good for a first crawfish tray; pick your own spice level.

food.name: Barbecue brisket
food.desc: Central Texas style: salt-and-pepper crusted brisket smoked over post oak for 12 hours, sold by the pound on butcher paper with pickles and onion.

places.name: Truth BBQ
places.note: Texas Monthly top-ranked brisket; get there early and save room for the cakes.

places.name: Pinkerton's Barbecue
places.note: Big beef ribs and peppery brisket; one of the city's most decorated smokehouses.

places.name: CorkScrew BBQ
places.note: Michelin-recognized family joint north of the city; worth the drive for the fatty end.

food.name: Kolache
food.desc: Texas-Czech breakfast pastry: pillowy sweet dough with fruit or cheese, or a sausage-stuffed klobasnek that Texans also call a kolache.

places.name: Kolache Shoppe
places.note: Long-running local bakery; sweet apricot and savory sausage-jalapeno-cheese both excellent.

places.name: Koffeteria
places.note: James Beard-nominated baker Vanarin Kuch's Asian-inflected kolaches, including beef pho.

places.name: Kolache Factory
places.note: Houston-founded chain; the reliable airport-run or road-trip breakfast option.

food.name: Banh mi
food.desc: Crackly baguette packed with pork, pate, pickled daikon and carrot, cilantro and jalapeno, from one of the largest Vietnamese communities in the US.

places.name: Les Ba'get
places.note: Modern Vietnamese cafe; lemongrass chicken banh mi and good iced coffee.

places.name: Cafe TH
places.note: Family-run spot near downtown known for grilled pork banh mi and pho.

places.name: Alpha Bakery and Deli
places.note: No-frills counter baking its own bread; among the best value sandwiches in town.

food.name: Vietnamese iced coffee
food.desc: Dark roast dripped slowly through a phin filter onto sweetened condensed milk, then poured over ice. Houston's unofficial afternoon fuel.

places.name: Le'Drip Coffee and Tea
places.note: Creative riffs like pandan bac xiu and ube cheese coffee alongside the classic ca phe sua da.

places.name: Long Coffee
places.note: Local favorite for a straight-up strong phin-dripped iced coffee.

food.name: Frozen margarita
food.desc: Tequila, lime and orange liqueur churned to a slush. The frozen machine version is a Texas invention and a Houston Tex-Mex ritual.

places.name: The Original Ninfa's on Navigation
places.note: The Ninfarita is the house benchmark; order it with the fajitas.

places.name: Hugo's
places.note: Chef Hugo Ortega's regional Mexican room with a deep tequila and mezcal list.

places.name: Candente
places.note: Houston's only Michelin-recommended Tex-Mex spot; the margarita program is a big reason.

landmarks: Space Center Houston
The official visitor center for NASA's Johnson Space Center lets visitors photograph real spacecraft and rockets.
Houston Museum of Natural Science
A major museum with dinosaur halls, gems, and a planetarium, popular for its grand Hermann Park setting.
San Jacinto Monument
The tallest masonry column monument in the world commemorates Texas's decisive independence battle and offers sweeping views from its observation deck.
Gerald D. Hines Waterwall Park
A dramatic 64-foot semicircular waterfall fountain in the Galleria area, beloved as a picturesque backdrop.
Discovery Green
This lively downtown urban park with its lake, art, and green lawns framed by skyscrapers is a favorite skyline photo spot.
Astrodome
The world's first domed sports stadium, nicknamed the 'Eighth Wonder of the World,' remains an iconic piece of Houston's architectural history.
Julia Ideson Building
This Spanish Renaissance-style historic library building is one of downtown Houston's most elegant architectural gems.
Rothko Chapel
A serene, minimalist chapel housing Mark Rothko's monumental paintings, renowned as a landmark of modern art and architecture.
Buffalo Bayou Park
This revitalized green space along the bayou offers striking views of the downtown Houston skyline reflected in the water.
Minute Maid Park
Home of the Houston Astros, this retractable-roof ballpark with its vintage train is a distinctive downtown landmark.

train.note: Houston has one of the thinnest train services of any large American city: Amtrak's Sunset Limited calls just three times a week in each direction, running between New Orleans and Los Angeles via San Antonio, El Paso and Tucson. The station is a small building on Washington Avenue northwest of downtown and the trains frequently call in the middle of the night, so check the timetable carefully before committing. There is no passenger rail to Mexico from anywhere in Texas. For Dallas, Austin or San Antonio the coach or a flight is far quicker than rail.

intl.to: Monterrey, San Luis Potosi, Guadalajara, Morelia & central Mexico

bus.note: Houston has three Tornado Bus terminals feeding a dense network of cross-border coaches, and Greyhound also runs into Monterrey and Nuevo Laredo. Journeys to Monterrey take around 12-14 hours, and you clear Mexican immigration at the border, so carry a passport and buy an FMM tourist card. The main Greyhound terminal is on Main Street south of downtown, on the METRORail Red Line, while FlixBus (https://www.flixbus.com/) and Megabus (https://us.megabus.com/) load curbside downtown and near the universities. Domestic times are roughly three hours to Austin, three to San Antonio and four to five to Dallas.

intl.to: Port Bolivar, Bolivar Peninsula (USA) - departs Galveston, about 50 miles southeast of Houston

ferry.note: The Port of Houston itself handles containers, tankers and cruise ships rather than scheduled passenger ferries, so the boat you actually use is the free state-run Galveston to Port Bolivar ferry about an hour's drive southeast. It carries cars as well as foot passengers, crosses in roughly 18 minutes and runs around the clock, no reservation possible - but queues can stretch to an hour or more on summer weekends and holidays. Dolphins often follow the boat, which makes it a popular free excursion in its own right.

half.name: Galveston
half.blurb: A Gulf Coast island city about an hour southeast of Houston, with a historic pier, beaches, and Moody Gardens.

half.name: Brazos Bend State Park
half.blurb: A wetland park roughly an hour southwest of Houston known for alligator sightings, hiking trails, and an observatory.

half.name: Sam Houston National Forest
half.blurb: A 163,000-acre pine forest north of the city with hiking, horseback riding, and camping along Lake Conroe.

half.name: Blue Bell Creameries (Brenham)
half.blurb: The original ice cream factory's visitor center in Brenham, about 90 minutes northwest, offers free weekday tours and tastings.

full.name: San Antonio
full.blurb: San Antonio's River Walk and the Alamo mission draw day-trippers roughly three hours west of Houston for history and riverside dining.
